title: Simplismart raises $14 Mn from Dallas Venture Capital, NVIDIA and others
summary:
AI inference infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.
The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its inference engine and orchestration platform, expand its cloud provider network and support its growth across North America and other global markets.
Entrackr had earlier reported on the deal, which values the company at around $100 million post money. Previously, Simplismart raised $7 million in a Series A round in October 2024.
Founded by Amritanshu Jain, Simplismart provides infrastructure that helps enterprises deploy and run AI models while optimising inference costs, latency and GPU utilisation. Its platform also enables cloud providers to convert their GPU capacity into AI services for enterprise customers.
The company said its annualised revenue run rate grew 14X over the past six months. Its customers include HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna and Ema, which use its platform for production workloads across video, voice, multimodal and enterprise AI applications.
Simplismart also works with cloud providers to offer managed AI inference services. At Yotta, its platform powers the serverless inference layer of Shakti Studio, which allows customers to run AI models without managing the underlying infrastructure.
Unlike inference providers that procure or reserve GPU capacity and resell it, Simplismart focuses on the software layer that enables third party GPU infrastructure to support production AI workloads. The company is also working with cloud providers and sovereign AI programmes across India, North America, the Middle East, Australia and East Asia.
The startup plans to use the new capital to further develop its inference and orchestration capabilities and build partnerships aimed at matching AI workloads with available GPU capacity across regions and cloud environments.

summary:

The round comprises primary capital for business growth and a secondary component that provides partial liquidity to early shareholders.
The fresh funds will be used to develop its agentic intelligence layer, expand its go-to-market operations for enterprise and global consumer brands, and strengthen its regional cloud infrastructure across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific, Live2.ai said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2024 by J Venkat, Neha Suyal and Yash Arora, Live2.ai provides a platform that connects social intelligence with campaign execution and commerce activation.
The platform helps brands monitor online conversations, plan and publish social media posts, track performance, manage audits and compliance for influencer and user-generated content, and convert rights-cleared content into shoppable experiences across digital and offline channels.
The Bengaluru-based startup said its platform combines a unified entity graph, multimodal AI and autonomous AI agents. It monitors brand conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X and review sites to help brands identify trends and inform business decisions.
Live2.ai offers three key capabilities: social intelligence for trend identification and campaign strategy; audit and compliance management for influencer and user-generated content; and social publishing and performance tracking across channels.
The platform also uses eight AI agents, including Crisis Detection, Trend Scout, Campaign Auditor and Autonomous Response, to support tasks across social intelligence, campaign management and customer engagement. These agents operate on a shared entity graph with governance controls and human review.
Live2.ai said it works with brands such as Henkel's Schwarzkopf, Salonory, Titan Brands and Shiseido. The company claims to serve more than 200 brands across the US, Europe and Southeast Asia.
The startup said its revenue grew fourfold in the past 12 months, with 90% of its revenue generated outside India.

summary:
Preventive healthcare startup Cent has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commons. The company has also acquired AI radiology platform Medsee.
The round saw participation from individual investors Arun Sarin, Srinivas Narayanan, Sharath Narayana, Aprameya Radhakrishna and Krishan Sridhar, Cent founder Shashank ND said in a LinkedIn post.
Founded by Shashank ND, who also founded healthcare platform Practo, Cent focuses on early disease detection through medical imaging, biomarkers and artificial intelligence (AI).
Over the past year, around 10,000 people have undergone screening through Cent's protocol. Of these, one in four had a finding that required medical attention, while one in 40 needed to consult a doctor immediately, the company said.
Cent's screening protocol combines full body MRI, low dose CT scans, DEXA, ECG, ECHO and over 100 biomarkers in a single session of around two hours. The startup operates its own centres in Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR, alongside its earlier network of partner diagnostic labs.
The fresh capital will be used to invest in hardware, AI and clinical research. The acquisition of Medsee will also strengthen Cent's AI capabilities, Shashank said.
Cent aims to conduct 10 million scans by 2035 and help save one million lives through early disease detection.
The startup is looking to address the gap in India's healthcare system, where several noncommunicable diseases are diagnosed at advanced stages. India has an estimated 101 million people living with diabetes and 136 million with prediabetes, while around 315 million people have hypertension, according to figures cited by Cent.
In September 2026, Practo elevated Shashank to managing director and executive chairman, while Jagnoor Singh was appointed CEO.

The company plans to expand its physical presence through Rotoris House, with plans to move beyond Delhi to Mumbai and New York.
Aakash Anand previously built and scaled beauty and personal care brand Bella Vita before exiting the business. Prerna Gupta leads Rotoris, with a focus on premium brand building and customer experience.

Founded this year by Anish Priyadarshi and Sanjeev Kumar, Nova Spectral AI develops lead free colloidal quantum dot (cQD) short wave infrared (SWIR) image sensor chips on standard silicon CMOS for defence intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) and physical AI applications.
The Bengaluru based startup said it is developing an indigenous quantum dot SWIR image sensor chip. The technology enables cameras to capture images in conditions where conventional cameras may struggle, including low light, haze and smoke. It can be used in drones, surveillance systems, robots and autonomous vehicles.
Nova Spectral AI uses CMOS compatible manufacturing processes and indium arsenide (InAs) colloidal quantum dots to develop infrared sensors. The company aims to reduce sensor costs by up to 100 times compared with conventional indium gallium arsenide (InGaAs) technology.
In defence, the technology could expand the use of SWIR imaging across drones and ISR platforms while reducing dependence on imported sensors. The company is also targeting applications in smartphones, wearables, robots and automobiles.
Colloidal quantum dot SWIR image sensors built on standard silicon CMOS are being explored as a way to make infrared imaging more affordable and scalable across applications that require vision in challenging conditions.
Another player in the space, SpectraGaze Systems, raised Rs 3.7 crore in seed funding led by GVFL to develop indigenous infrared detectors, optical imaging sensors and electro optical payloads for space and defence applications.

title: MakeMyTrip returns to profit in Q2 FY27; gross bookings grow 21%
summary:
MakeMyTrip returned to profitability in Q2 FY27 as growth in hotels, bus ticketing and ancillary services offset pressure on air travel. The Nasdaq-listed company reported a net profit of $1.8 million for the quarter ended September 2026, compared with a loss of $5.7 million a year earlier, while gross bookings rose 20.9% year-on-year in constant currency to $2.72 billion.
Revenue increased 2.5% to $235.2 million from $229.3 million, although growth stood at 11.2% after adjusting for currency movements. The Indian rupee depreciated approximately 10% against the US dollar during the quarter, affecting reported revenue growth. 
MakeMyTrip also cited elevated airfares and subdued international long-haul travel, partly offset by strong domestic demand. 
Adjusted operating profit rose to $46.2 million from $44.2 million, while adjusted net profit before tax increased 26.9% to $46.2 million. Adjusted EBITDA stood at $51.5 million, up 6.4% year-on-year. However, the return to a small reported net profit came alongside slower growth in reported revenue than in gross bookings.
Hotels and packages remained the largest contributor to adjusted margin, which rose 20.2% in constant currency to $116.8 million. Standalone hotel room nights grew 18.6%, supported by domestic hotel bookings that increased more than 20%. The company said demand for domestic leisure trips, shorter holidays and pilgrimage travel supported the segment.
Air ticketing adjusted margin increased 14.3% to $108.6 million in constant currency, despite a 7.2% decline in reported revenue from the segment to $56.7 million. Management attributed the pressure to higher fares and constrained airline capacity. It said the business maintained market share and improved unit economics through ancillary services.
Bus ticketing was another growth area. Its adjusted margin rose 29% to $45.1 million, while revenue increased 16.6% in reported terms to $19.4 million. Revenue from other businesses, including ancillary services, grew 21.6% to $21.2 million.
MakeMyTrip is also expanding its AI assistant, Myra. It handled more than 90,000 conversations daily during the quarter, resolved over 53% of post-booking flight and hotel queries, and assisted with more than 3,000 completed bookings per day. Customers using Myra completed around 1.7 times more bookings than non-users, according to the company.
Despite the quarterly turnaround, first-half net profit fell 45.8% to $10.9 million, while free cash flow declined 19.8% to $67.1 million. The figures suggest that the recovery in quarterly earnings has yet to translate into stronger year-to-date profitability.

summary:
Trading platform Mochatrade has raised $5.5 million in a seed funding round led by CoinFund, with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Zero Knowledge Ventures, among others. Its earlier backers include Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
The fresh funds will be used to develop its trading engine and risk infrastructure, as well as expand its reach among active Indian traders, Mochatrade said in a press release.
Founded this year by Utkarsh Sinha, Parth Maheshwari and Chetan Manda, Mochatrade is a trading platform for Indian users that combines UPI-based funding and rupee balances with access to contracts linked to US stocks, indices and commodities.
According to the company, users can fund their accounts through UPI and view margins, or the money set aside for trades, as well as profits and losses in rupees. Users can take long or short positions through perpetual futures contracts linked to US company prices without opening a US brokerage account. These contracts have no fixed expiry, and users do not own the underlying shares. Leverage allows users to take larger positions with less upfront capital, but also amplifies potential losses.
Through its Indian operating entity, Mochatrade is registered with the Financial Intelligence Unit India (FIU-IND) as a Virtual Digital Asset Service Provider and a reporting entity for anti-money laundering purposes.
The platform said its waitlist has crossed 25,000 sign-ups. However, it has not announced a public launch date. Users can join the waitlist on its website for early access updates.
Mochatrade also plans to introduce contracts linked to select pre-IPO companies, US stock options and social trading features, subject to applicable laws and regulatory approvals. The company said its markets are designed to offer continuous access and real-time settlement, subject to liquidity, asset availability and risk controls.

title: Snapdeal parent AceVector posts Rs 151 Cr revenue and Rs 17.6 Cr loss in Q2 FY27
summary:
AceVector, the parent company of e-commerce platform Snapdeal, has reported its first quarterly results since its listing earlier this month. The company’s revenue rose 17% year-on-year to cross Rs 150 crore in Q2 FY27, while its losses stood at Rs 17.6 crore.
According to its unaudited quarterly results, AceVector’s operating revenue stood at Rs 151.2 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 129.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Snapdeal’s marketplace business accounted for the largest share of AceVector’s operating revenue at 57%, with revenue of Rs 86.2 crore, up 15% year-on-year. Its e-commerce enablement SaaS platform, Unicommerce, contributed Rs 59 crore, while consumer brands added Rs 6 crore to operating revenue.
Including Rs 2.6 crore in non-operating income, AceVector’s total income stood at Rs 153.8 crore in Q2 FY27.
For the first half of FY27, AceVector’s consolidated revenue grew 17% year-on-year to Rs 285.5 crore, supported by growth across Snapdeal and Unicommerce. Snapdeal’s revenue rose 15% to Rs 164.4 crore, while Unicommerce recorded a 15% increase to Rs 110.4 crore.
Snapdeal’s fashion net merchandise value (NMV) rose 31% year-on-year to Rs 407.6 crore in H1 FY27. Its annual transacting customer base grew 12% to 130.8 lakh, while app-delivered units increased 23% to 133.6 lakh. During the period, the company also launched an AI solutions suite for customers, sellers and creators, with features for product discovery, personalised recommendations and seller support.
Logistics expenses remained AceVector’s largest cost at Rs 71.4 crore, up 20% year-on-year. The expense accounted for over 42% of its total expenditure. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 46 crore during the quarter.
AceVector’s total expenditure rose over 21% year-on-year to Rs 168.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 138.7 crore in the year-ago quarter. The faster growth in expenses compared with revenue led to an 85% increase in losses to Rs 17.6 crore, which included Rs 1.3 crore in exceptional items.
AceVector made a weak stock market debut on the stock market, with its shares listed at an 11.5% discount to the IPO price of Rs 32. The stock opened at Rs 28.32 on the NSE and Rs 28.30 on the BSE, despite the Rs 420 crore IPO receiving around 5 times subscription. 
The issue comprised a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 133 crore, with a price band of Rs 30 to Rs 32 per share.
At the end of Monday’s trading session, AceVector’s shares closed at Rs 20.92, with a total market capitalization of Rs 1,138 crore.

title: WeWork India’s Q2 FY27 revenue rises 34% to Rs 768 Cr, profit jumps over 3X
summary:
Managed office space provider WeWork India has announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY27). The company posted 33.8% year-on-year growth in operating revenue during the period, while profit surged over 3X. 
WeWork India’s revenue from operations rose 33.8% year-on-year to Rs 768 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 574 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.


For the first half of FY27, The company’s revenue from operations increased 30.8% to Rs 1,452 crore from Rs 1,110 crore in H1 FY26.
Income from managed workspace and allied services remained the company’s sole source of operating revenue. It also reported Rs 18 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 786 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 585.5 crore in Q2 FY26.
On the expenditure front, depreciation and amortisation related to leases remained the largest cost head at Rs 314 crore, up 35.9% year-on-year. Finance costs increased 14.4% to Rs 175 crore, while employee benefit expenses also increased 16.7% to Rs 56 crore. Operating expenses surged 52% to Rs 194.5 crore, while other expenses climbed 44.7% to Rs 27.5 crore.

As a result, WeWork India’s total expenses increased 32.5% to Rs 767 crore in Q2 FY27.
At the bottom line, WeWork India reported a profit of Rs 20.44 crore in Q2 FY27, up 219.4% from Rs 6.4 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal. For the first half of FY27, the company posted a profit of Rs 16.37 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 7.74 crore in H1 FY26.

At the end of Monday’s trading session, WeWork India shares closed at Rs 622.55 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 8,751 crore.

title: Paytm reports Rs 2,648 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; profit jumps 10.7X
summary:
Fintech firm One97 Communications, which operates Paytm, announced its financial results for the second quarter of FY27 on Monday. The company’s profit increased 10.7 times year-on-year to Rs 225 crore, while revenue from operations grew 28.5% in the quarter.
According to its unaudited quarterly results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Paytm’s operating revenue stood at Rs 2,648 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,061 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Payment services remained Paytm’s largest revenue contributor, with revenue from the segment rising over 25% year-on-year to Rs 1,434 crore in Q2 FY27. The segment accounted for more than 54% of the company’s operating revenue. Revenue from financial services distribution and marketing services stood at Rs 912 crore and Rs 287 crore, respectively.
Paytm also earned Rs 182 crore from non-operating sources during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 2,830 crore in Q2 FY27.
On a sequential basis, Paytm’s revenue increased 8% from Rs 2,448 crore in Q1 FY27.
Payment processing charges remained Paytm’s largest expense in Q2 FY27, at nearly 32% of its total costs. This expense rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 805 crore. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 759 crore, up over 14% from the same quarter last year.
Marketing expenses increased 59% year-on-year to Rs 194 crore in Q2 FY27. Software, cloud, communication, legal, cashback, and other overhead expenses drove total expenditure to Rs 2,531 crore during the quarter, compared to Rs 2,062 crore in the year-ago period.
Paytm’s net profit surged 10.7 times year-on-year to Rs 225 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
For the half year ended September 2026, the Vijay Shekhar Sharma-led firm reported operating revenue of Rs 5,096 crore, while its net profit more than doubled to Rs 491 crore.
At the end of today’s trading session, Paytm’s share price closed at Rs 1,654.7, with a total market capitalization of Rs 1,06,250 crore or ($11.2 billion).

title: Nazara returns to profit in Q2 FY27; advertising accounts for 54% of total cost
summary:
Nazara Technologies, a gaming and sports media company, reported a 52.7% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27 and returned to profitability despite a 3.6-fold jump in advertising expenses.
The company’s operating revenue increased 52.7% to Rs 803 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 526 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange.


On a half-yearly basis, Nazara’s operating revenue grew 20.2% to Rs 1,232 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 1,025 crore in H1 FY26.
Gaming remained the largest revenue contributor, accounting for 81.7% of operating revenue. Revenue from the segment jumped 2.22X to Rs 656 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 296 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Meanwhile, revenue from the ad-tech business declined 13.9% to Rs 124 crore from Rs 144 crore. The esports segment also reported a 73.6% drop in revenue to Rs 23 crore from Rs 87 crore during the same period.
Advertising and business promotion emerged as the largest cost for the firm, which surged 3.6 times to Rs 417 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 116 crore in Q2 FY26. Employee benefit expenses increased 9.2% to Rs 85.21 crore from Rs 78 crore during the same period.
Content, event and web server expenses declined 58.3% to Rs 66.75 crore from Rs 160 crore, while depreciation expenses rose 20.6% to Rs 73.56 crore from Rs 61 crore. Commission expenses fell 2% to Rs 50 crore from Rs 51 crore, whereas other expenses increased 11% to Rs 75.5 crore from Rs 68 crore.
As a result, Nazara’s total expenditure increased 43.8% to Rs 768 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 534 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year. 

Despite the revenue growth, The Mumbai based company returned to profit Rs 35.36 crore compared from around Rs 34 crore loss in Q2FY26. The company reported a net loss of Rs 47.11 crore in H1 FY27, compared to a net profit of Rs 17.41 crore in the first half of FY26.

At the close of trading, Nazara Technologies’ shares settled at Rs 399.95, giving the company a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 16,402 crore.

summary:
Direct-to-consumer (D2C) apparel brand ReplyAll has raised Rs 9.7 crore in pre-Series A funding round co-led by Sadev Ventures and Atom XVII. The round also saw participation from ISV and Long View Ventures, along with existing investors Sparrow and Antler, and a group of angel investors.
The brand had previously secured Rs 6.8 crore ($750K) in its first funding round led by Sparrow Capital and Antler India, with participation from Bharat Founders Fund, DeVC, and several D2C founders in Dec. last year.
The proceeds will be used to invest in fabric research and development, product design, new categories, and the brand’s retail and community presence, ReplyAll said in a press release.
Launched in 2025 by Rushabh Sanghavi, ReplyAll offers performance wear and everyday apparel designed for work, travel, workouts and casual wear.
The Bengaluru-based brand focuses on versatile styling, functional details and material innovation to develop clothing for everyday use.
According to the company, its Temperform™ fabric, used in the Coolest Tee, is designed to help manage heat during everyday activities and sports. Its Flexknit™ material offers stretch and wrinkle resistance in trousers designed for work, travel and casual wear. ReplyAll plans to invest in further fabric research and expand its product categories.
The company said it has recorded month-on-month revenue growth over the past seven months. Its first three product launches, the Coolest Tee, All-In Pants and Stepwise Tee, sold out, while repeat customers account for 40% of its revenue.

title: Social gaming startup Matiks raises $10 Mn in Pre-Series A led by General Catalyst
summary:
Bengaluru-based social gaming startup Matiks has raised $10 million in a Pre-Series A funding round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Ronnie Screwvala and existing investors Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners and Untitled Ventures.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its international presence, develop new games and social experiences, and launch an AI-powered game creation platform that will allow users to build and publish games without coding.
Founded in 2024 by Sudhanshu Bhatia, Sushant and Mohan, Matiks started as a mental maths game and has since expanded into a social gaming platform offering games across mathematics, memory, logic and puzzles. The platform allows users to compete against friends, participate in daily challenges and track their progress.
In September 2026, 2.2 million users played 48 million games on the platform. Its daily active users have more than doubled since June to over 300,000, with the company also seeing early traction in markets such as Japan, the US and South Korea.
The company recently launched SNAC, an endless feed of single-player puzzles, which has contributed to longer user sessions, according to Matiks.
Matiks plans to initially focus on the US market before expanding into other major international markets. It will also invest in engineering, artificial intelligence, product development, game design and growth.
The company is also developing an AI-powered game creation engine that will enable users to create, publish and share their own brain games across multiple formats.
In August 2025, Matiks raised $3.1 million in a Pre-Series A round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, with participation from Info Edge Ventures and angel investors, including boAt co-founder Aman Gupta and Unacademy co-founders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini, among others.

The company creates proprietary datasets from de-identified clinical data to support medical research, drug development and the training and evaluation of healthcare AI models. Its platform also incorporates workflows tailored to individual healthcare providers and their data privacy protocols.

summary:
Entrackr’s D2C community initiative, The Spur, held its second edition in Bengaluru on October 23, bringing together direct-to-consumer (D2C) founders to discuss the challenges of building and scaling consumer brands.
Held at The Bier Library and supported by PhonePe Payment Gateway, the gathering moved away from conventional startup events by skipping panel discussions, presentations and pitches in favour of open conversations about the realities of running a business.
The discussions focused on what works when building a brand, what does not, and what founders would do differently based on their experiences. The informal format encouraged participants to share practical lessons from their entrepreneurial journeys.

The Bengaluru edition brought together more than 30 founders and business leaders from across the D2C ecosystem, including Puspen Maity of Technosport, Ujwal Sutaria of TDV Partners, Ramprasad Shastry of DriveU, Kavin KK of Agrizy, Surbhi Bhatia of The Mom Store, Adarsh J. Srivastava of DeHaat, Sharath Loganathan of Ninjacart, Pratyush Giri, Saras Agarwal of Navora Wellness, Sachin Nandwana of BigHaat, Shivam Dang of Shadowfax and Shagun Dwivedi of Deconstruct.
The Bengaluru event followed the first edition of The Spur, held in Gurugram on September 25. The gathering brought together more than 40 founders and 10 investors from the NCR D2C ecosystem to discuss building and scaling consumer businesses.

Designed as a community-building initiative rather than a conventional networking event, The Spur has no fixed discussion topics or commercial agenda. It encourages founders to speak openly about their journeys, including setbacks and lessons that are often missing from public accounts of startup growth.

title: Ather Energy shares jump 14% on Q2 profit turnaround; capacity set to expand
summary:
Shares of Ather Energy jumped around 14% to Rs 1,575 per share on Monday after the electric two-wheeler maker reported a consolidated net profit in Q2 FY27, compared with a loss in the year-ago period. The company also announced plans to expand its annual production capacity by 2.25 lakh units across its Hosur and AURIC facilities to meet growing demand.
Ather Energy reported a consolidated profit after tax of Rs 1.26 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, against a loss of Rs 154 crore in Q2 FY26. Its consolidated total income rose 62% year-on-year to Rs 1,527 crore, while vehicle volumes increased 42% to 93,211 units, according to the company’s press release.
The company posted an EBITDA of Rs 74.2 crore during the quarter, marking its second consecutive EBITDA-positive quarter. Its EBITDA margin improved to 4.9% from negative 9.6% a year earlier, supported by higher volumes, product mix and pricing decisions.
Ather said customer enquiries rose 109% year-on-year to around 10 lakh in Q2 FY27, while pre-orders more than doubled to 1.8 lakh units. Its Hosur facility operated at 98% capacity utilisation during peak production in the quarter.
To cater to the growing demand, Ather plans to increase annual production capacity at Hosur from 4.2 lakh units to 4.95 lakh units by December 2026. Its upcoming AURIC facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is scheduled to begin commercial production in phases from December 2026, with an initial annual capacity of 5 lakh units. The company plans to expand this to 6.5 lakh units by Q2 FY28.
The capacity expansion will require an investment of approximately Rs 122 crore, taking Ather’s combined installed annual production capacity to around 11.4 lakh units by Q2 FY28.
During the quarter, Ather also launched Konarc, its first scooter built on the new EL platform. Unveiled at its Community Day event in August, the scooter focuses on everyday comfort and convenience. It features a metal body, an adjustable backrest, keyless access and a new Bedrock battery backed by a 10-year warranty.
Brokerages have also remained bullish on Ather. In August, CLSA retained its ‘Outperform’ rating on the company with a target price of Rs 1,600, citing strong volume growth, robust bookings, upcoming capacity expansion and the launch of its EL platform.

summary:

Higher electric two-wheeler sales and an increase in other income helped Ather Energy turn profitable with a net profit of Rs 1.3 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 154 crore in the year-ago quarter. The company more than doubled its vehicle sales to 93,211 units from 52,961 units in Q2 FY26.

title: Kapiva crosses Rs 460 Cr revenue in FY26; targets EBITDA profitability by Q4 FY27
summary:
Following 50% growth in FY25, Ayurveda wellness brand Kapiva continued its growth momentum in FY26, with its revenue crossing Rs 460 crore. The company also managed to keep its losses largely stable despite higher spending on marketing and other operating costs, while its margins improved after excluding employee stock option (ESOP) expenses.
Kapiva’s revenue from operations grew 36.5% year-on-year to Rs 464 crore in FY26 from Rs 340 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). Including non-operating income of Rs 10 crore, its total income stood at Rs 474 crore.
Founded in 2015, Kapiva offers Ayurvedic nutrition and wellness products across categories such as diabetes management, liver health, hormonal balance, energy and sports nutrition. Sales of its products remained the company’s sole source of operating revenue.

Advertising and promotional expenses remained Kapiva’s largest cost component, accounting for nearly 48% of its total expenditure. The expense increased 39.8% to Rs 260 crore in FY26 from Rs 186 crore in the previous fiscal year.
The firm’s procurement costs rose 22.6% to Rs 117 crore, while employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 78 crore. Higher spending across these and other heads, including legal, technology and freight, pushed its total expenditure up 31.2% to Rs 547 crore in FY26 from Rs 417 crore in FY25.
Despite the increase in expenses, Kapiva’s losses remained broadly stable at Rs 72 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 69 crore a year earlier. Its EBITDA margin, excluding ESOP expenses of Rs 7.85 crore, improved to -14.8% in FY26 from -18.7% in FY25. At the unit level, the company spent Rs 1.18 to earn every rupee of operating revenue.
Kapiva has also expanded its product portfolio and distribution network, with investments in new categories such as liver care, cholesterol management and women’s hormonal health, along with infrastructure for offline distribution.
“During the last year, Kapiva has made significant investments in creating new categories (Liver Care, Cholesterol, Women’s Hormonal Health) and building infrastructure for offline distribution. These investments are likely to deliver substantial leverage in coming years which helps drive profitability,” a company spokesperson said.
The investments are reflected in the company’s category and channel growth. In FY26, its lifestyle diseases category grew 114% year-on-year, followed by daily wellness at 66% and women’s health at 21%. The sports nutrition and energy category grew 5% during the period.
According to Kapiva, offline sales led channel growth, increasing 81% year-on-year in FY26. Revenue from marketplaces rose 34%, while its direct-to-consumer (D2C) channel grew 21%. The company’s average order value on its D2C platform stood at around Rs 1,200, with repeat purchases accounting for nearly 55% of its D2C revenue.
Kapiva said its current annual recurring revenue (ARR) is around Rs 650-700 crore and that it expects to achieve a low-single-digit positive EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27.
The company has raised around $90 million in funding to date, including a $60 million Series D round led by 360 ONE Asset and Vertex Growth.
Kapiva competes with wellness brands such as Wellbeing Nutrition, which reported revenue of Rs 244 crore in FY26, along with Innovacare and Gynoveda, which are yet to report FY26 numbers.
Kapiva’s recent financial performance points to a business that has expanded rapidly over the past two years. After growing its revenue by 50% in FY25, the company added Rs 124 crore to its operating revenue in FY26. Its revenue has increased by around 93% in two years, from approximately Rs 240 crore in FY24 to Rs 464 crore in FY26. While marketing expenses continue to weigh on profitability, strong growth in offline sales and newer product categories, along with repeat purchases on its D2C platform, could support operating leverage as the company scales. Its target of turning EBITDA-positive by Q4 FY27 will depend on how effectively it converts this growth into improved margins.

title: Yes Madam’s revenue jumps over 2X to Rs 195 Cr in FY26
summary:
Home salon services platform Yes Madam more than doubled its operating revenue to Rs 195 crore in FY26 for the second straight year, taking its revenue to over 4X in two years, but slipped into losses amid higher employee and advertising costs during FY26.
The company’s revenue from operations jumped 2.07X to Rs 195 crore in FY26 compared with Rs 94 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2016, Noida-based Yes Madam is an at-home beauty and wellness services platform that offers services such as haircuts, facials, waxing and massages through its app and website. The company has also launched instant salon and spa services, enabling customers to book at-home services within 30 minutes.

Revenue from the sale of services, which includes commission income earned as an agent between service professionals and end customers, along with subscription and royalty income, contributed 51% of Yes Madam’s operating revenue. This segment grew 2.3 times to reach Rs 100 crore mark in FY26. 
Revenue from product sales rose 90% to Rs 95 crore from Rs 50 crore during the same period, accounting for the remaining 49% of operating revenue.
On the expense side, advertising and promotional expenses emerged as the largest cost for the firm, which surged 2.31X to Rs 67 crore in the last fiscal year from Rs 29 crore in FY25, while the cost of materials consumed rose 90.6% to Rs 61 crore. 
Employee benefit expenses also more than doubled to Rs 43 crore, while freight costs also increased 164.2% to Rs 4.28 crore during the same period.
Other expenses, including information technology, rent and legal and professional charges, collectively added Rs 27.7 crore in FY26. As a result, Yes Madam’s total expenditure jumped 2.21X to Rs 203 crore in FY26 from Rs 92 crore
Noida-based Yes Madam reported a net loss of Rs 7.75 crore in FY26, compared with a net profit of Rs 1.83 crore in FY25, as expenses grew faster than revenue. Its EBITDA margin also declined to -3.89% from 2.18% during the same period.

On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 1.04 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 0.98 in FY25. 
At the end of March 2026, the firm had cash and bank balances of Rs 2.03 crore, while total current assets increased to Rs 32.34 crore from Rs 21.41 crore a year earlier.
Yes Madam remained bootstrapped for nearly a decade before raising its first institutional funding of Rs 50 crore from Info Edge at a valuation of Rs 750 crore earlier this year. According to media reports, the company is now in talks to raise Rs 250 crore from Xponentia Capital Partners, Riverwalk Holdings and other investors at a valuation of around Rs 1,900 crore.

According to Yes Madam’s press release, its revenue grew 11% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 79.4 crore in Q2 FY27, while NTV rose 12% to Rs 165.8 crore. On a year-on-year basis, revenue and NTV grew 69% and 75%, respectively. Over two years, revenue increased 3.9 times and NTV 3.5 times, taking their annualised run rates to Rs 402 crore and Rs 836 crore, respectively.

The fresh funds will be utilized to strengthen technology and product, onboard more high-quality operators, and expand beyond Rishikesh, starting with Manali and Bir, and invest in content, organic discovery and distribution partnerships, Bucketlistt said in a press release.
Launched last year by Shubham Makhecha, Nitant Desai and Divyam Shah, Bucketlistt.com is a platform to discover and book experiences across India. Its operator platform, OkGhumo, is an operating system for experience providers that digitises bookings, inventory, agents and payments.
The Ahmedabad based startup helps travellers discover and book verified travel experiences, from skydiving in Mt. Abu and front row seats at the Ganga Aarti in Rishikesh to dinner with royal families in Jaipur.
The company launched in Rishikesh in December 2025. Alongside the marketplace, it runs OkGhumo, a platform that experience providers use to manage bookings, inventory, agents, payments and daily operations.
In the last 10 months, Bucketlistt.com and OkGhumo claimed to have together managed more than Rs 22.5 crore in bookings, while Bucketlistt.com has served more than 12,000 customers. About one in five of its customers now comes through word of mouth.
Launched in March 2026, OkGhumo has served more than 50,000 customers. Leading adventure operators in Rishikesh use it daily to manage bookings, inventory, agent settlements and payments, replacing calls, WhatsApp and spreadsheets. It also provides Bucketlistt.com with live inventory, allowing travellers to receive instant and reliable confirmations. The company now plans to replicate this model across multiple cities.
It competes with other players in the space, such as Klook, GetYourGuide, Alyve and Viator.

The fresh capital will be used to scale up production of AI-powered camera systems and develop technology that enables drones to navigate without GPS, Paar Autonomy said in a press release.
Founded in June 2024 by Vignesh Sivaram Jayaraman, Paar Autonomy builds camera systems and AI software for drones and other unmanned defence platforms. Its products focus on the perception layer for unmanned aerial, ground and maritime vehicles, including drones, rovers and boats.
The company’s capabilities include edge-based AI, GPS and GNSS-independent visual-inertial navigation, and gyro-stabilised, multi-sensor gimbal camera payloads. These technologies are designed to support operations in GPS-denied and communication-contested environments.
Paar Autonomy also uses AI models to enable real-time environmental interpretation, situational awareness and target tracking for autonomous operations.
Its product portfolio includes the Sentinel series, comprising Sentinel 1, Sentinel 2, Sentinel Nano, Sentinel Nano Dark and Sentinel Nano Dual.
The company primarily caters to defence applications such as border surveillance and tactical tracking. It also serves civilian use cases, including industrial inspection, infrastructure monitoring and disaster response.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 19- Oct 24]
summary:
This week, 15 Indian startups raised $133.9 million across 4 growth-stage deals, 10 early-stage deals, and 1 undisclosed round. The week also saw 5 key appointments. 
In contrast, 30 startups had collectively secured about $302.85 million in the previous week.

[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $86.2 million across four deals this week, led by Even Healthcare, which secured $50 million in a Series B round led by existing investor Khosla Ventures. Premium menswear brand The Pant Project raised Rs 109 crore in a Series B round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investments India, with participation from existing investor Sorin Investments.
Battery-swapping startup Battery Smart raised close to Rs 100 crore from an existing investor to expand its network for electric two- and three-wheelers. Meanwhile, rural healthcare startup CureBay secured around Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C round led by IvyCap Ventures.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $47.7 million across 10 deals this week, led by AI startup AuxoAI, which secured $20.7 million in a Series A round led by NTTVC. Home and kitchen brand Chapter Home raised Rs 63 crore through a mix of equity and debt from Bessemer Venture Partners, Stride Ventures, influencer Tanmay Bhat and family offices.
Travel platform TravClan raised $5 million from online retailer Flipkart and investment firm August One, along with debt financing from Trifecta Capital. Hunar.AI, an AI-powered frontline workforce platform, secured Rs 40 crore in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures. AI startup Vectorial raised $3 million in a round led by SenseAI Ventures, while voice AI platform Karta AI secured $3 million in a seed round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill.
Other startups that raised funding this week included Japanese food and beverage business Harajuku, customer-first travel platform Onto, lab-grown diamond jewellery brand So/Facet, spacetech startup SpectraGaze and logistics startup Raaho.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led startup funding activity with seven deals during the week, followed by Mumbai and Delhi-NCR with three deals each. Bhubaneswar and Ahmedabad also recorded funding deals.

AI startups led the sectors with 4 deals, followed by e-commerce startups which grabbed 3 deals. Meanwhile healthtech, travel tech, EV, Foodtech, spacetech and  logistics also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with 4 deals, followed by Series A and Series B startups which grabbed 3 deals and 2 deals respectively. Pre-seed, Series C, pre-Series C and pre-Series A also recorded  deals this week.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding declined 56% to $133.9 million from $302.85 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $234 million across 22 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Fractal Analytics has appointed Shilpa Kedia as its chief financial officer (CFO) to oversee global finance operations, with a focus on profitable growth, capital allocation and investments in AI research, platforms and products. IVS Group has named Atish Bhatia as group chief marketing officer (CMO) and head of IVS Fashion. Meanwhile, Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, has elevated Vipul Maheshwari to chief product and technology officer (CPTO).
[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ Ultraviolette launches X-47 Venom electric motorcycle, introduces new VX-100 platform
Bengaluru-based electric mobility startup Ultraviolette Automotive has launched the X-47 Venom electric motorcycle at an introductory price of Rs 2.65 lakh, alongside its new 100V VX-100 platform. The first motorcycle built on the new architecture, the X-47 Venom is designed to improve performance, energy efficiency, charging speed and safety while reducing weight. Bookings opened on October 22, with the introductory price available to the first 5,000 customers. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in November 2026 through Ultraviolette’s UV Space Stations across India.
▪️ Eternal’s Dark.ai aims to offer encrypted AI chats, targets launch this year
Eternal is preparing to launch Dark.ai, a global AI platform focused on privacy and encrypted conversations, later this year. The platform will use fine-tuned open-weight models hosted on its own infrastructure and offer end-to-end encryption. Dark.ai aims to address concerns around data retention, third-party access and the use of sensitive conversations, claiming that even the company cannot read users’ chats.
[Q2 FY27 results this week]

[News flash this week]
▪️ PhonePe rebrands Share.Market as PhonePe Invest
PhonePe has rebranded its stock broking platform Share.Market as PhonePe Invest, bringing it under the PhonePe brand alongside its payments, lending and insurance services to expand its reach among existing users. The company has also launched Portfolio Optimiser, a portfolio intelligence tool that offers research-backed Hold, Monitor or Sell ratings across linked demat accounts and a one-click rebalancing feature to identify underperforming assets and sector concentration risks.
▪️Zetwerk shares list at over 5% premium in stock market debut
Bengaluru-based Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses made a positive stock market debut on Friday, with shares listing at Rs 159.25 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), a 5.5% premium over the IPO issue price of Rs 151 per share.
▪️ Blacksmith raises $66 Mn at $1 Bn valuation led by Sequoia
AI code testing platform Blacksmith has raised $66 million in a Series C funding round led by Sequoia Capital at a valuation of $1 billion. The round also saw participation from Premji Invest and existing investors Peak XV Partners, Google Ventures (GV) and Y Combinator, taking its total funding to $125 million.
▪️Mygate, Adonmo set to merge; Eternal to hold 4.4% stake in combined entity
Eternal, formerly Zomato, will acquire a 4.4% stake in Mygate, valued at Rs 156 crore, through a share swap involving its entire holding in Adonmo. The transaction forms part of the proposed merger between Mygate and Adonmo, following which Adonmo will cease to exist as a separate entity. Eternal had invested Rs 112 crore in Adonmo in January 2022.
▪️ Kissht gets BSE, NSE nod for Rs 832 Cr fundraise
Kissht, operated by OnEMI Technology Solutions, has received in-principle approvals from the BSE and NSE to raise Rs 832.2 crore through a preferential issue of up to 2.65 crore shares at Rs 314.11 apiece. The fundraise, approved by the board in September and shareholders in October, will see participation from 34 investors, including Axis Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, MIT, WhiteOak, 360 ONE, Groww Mutual Fund and Bandhan Mutual Fund.

title: Unicommerce posts Rs 59 Cr revenue and Rs 6.4 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
summary:
E-commerce enablement SaaS platform Unicommerce continued its growth trajectory in the latest quarter, reporting a 15% year-on-year increase in revenue and a 10.7% rise in net profit during Q2 FY27.
The company’s revenue from operation increased to Rs 59.10 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 51.38crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal. according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.


For the first half of FY27, Unicommerce’s revenue from operations increased 14.7% to Rs 110.45 crore from Rs 96.32 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal.

Unicommerce also earned Rs 1.56 crore from other income, taking its total income to Rs 60.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 52.2 crore in Q2 FY26.

On the expense side, employee benefit expenses rose 23.4% to Rs 20.90 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 16.94 crore in Q2 FY26, while server hosting costs surged 41.5% to Rs 1.91 crore. Depreciation expenses increased 7.5% to Rs 2.15 crore, while finance costs declined 5% to Rs 19 lakh. Other expenses grew 15.5% to Rs 27.67 crore.

Overall, total expenses increased 18.9% to Rs 52.83 crore during the quarter from Rs 44.45 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal.

At the end, the Gurugram-based firm reported a net profit of Rs 6.40 crore in Q2 FY27, up 10.7% from Rs 5.78 crore in Q2 FY26. Its net profit grew 14.5% to Rs 11.07 crore in Q2FY27  from Rs 9.67 crore in Q1 FY27.

Unicommerce shares closed at Rs 76.09 apiece at the end of Friday’s trading session, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 896 crore.

title: Garuda Aerospace’s FY26 revenue jumps 67% to Rs 206 Cr; profit rise 42%
summary:
Drone technology startup Garuda Aerospace reported a strong 67% year-on-year revenue growth in FY26 while maintaining profitability, with net profit at Rs 26 crore as the Chennai-based company is preparing to go public soon as it recently received SEBI nod for Rs 1,000 crore IPO.
Garuda’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 206 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026,compared to Rs 123.5 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).


Garuda Aerospace designs and manufactures drones for applications across agriculture, defence, infrastructure, mining and disaster management. Besides drone manufacturing, the firm also offers Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) and operates a DGCA-approved remote pilot training programme. 
Revenue from sale of services surged 84.1% to Rs 106.46 crore in FY26 from Rs 57.83 crore in FY25, while revenue from sale of products grew 66.2% to Rs 99.50 crore from Rs 59.85 crore during the same period.
On the expense front, the cost of materials, remains the largest expense component, rose 62% to Rs 117 crore in FY26 from Rs 72.21 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses declined 16.2% to Rs 8 crore from Rs 9.55 crore.
Legal and professional charges surged 94.6% to Rs 12.88 crore from Rs 6.62 crore. Other overheads such as impairment loss on financial assets, depreciation & amortization expenses, travelling added another Rs 34.12 crore to the total cost.
Overall, Garuda’s total expenses grew 73.7% to Rs 172 crore in the last fiscal year compared to Rs 99 crore in FY25.


Despite the increase in costs, the company reported a 41.5% increase in net profit to Rs 26 crore in FY26 from Rs 18.37 crore in FY25. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood and EBITDA margin stood  at 14.71% and 18.97% respectively.

On a unit level, Garuda spent Rs 0.83 to generate every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared to Rs 0.80 in FY25. 

At the end of March 2026, the firm’s total current assets increased to Rs 303 crore from Rs 176 crore, while its cash and bank balance stood at Rs 5.2 crore.
Garuda Aerospace pre-filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI through the confidential route in April. The proposed Rs 1,000 crore IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 750 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 250 crore by existing shareholders.

title: Harajuku Tokyo Café raises $3 Mn in pre-Series A led by Zero W
summary:
Harajuku Tokyo Café, the Japanese food and beverage business operating Harajuku Tokyo Café and Harajuku Bakehouse, has raised $3 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Zero W.
Existing seed investors Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC participated in the round with follow-on investments. New investors include Blume Founders Fund, Brijesh Parekh Family Office, Rahul Jain, co-founder of Epigamia, and others.
The company had previously raised $2 million (Rs 19 crore) in a seed funding round co-led by IAN and Samved VC in August 2025, with participation from LetsVenture and venture debt fund Capitar Ventures.
The proceeds will be used to fund the next phase of growth. The company aims to achieve Rs 100 crore in revenue in the current financial year, Harajuku Tokyo Café said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Gaurav Kanwar, Harajuku operates two food and beverage concepts across Delhi NCR and Mumbai. Harajuku Tokyo Café is a full-service dining format featuring conveyor-belt sushi and Tokyo-inspired interiors.
Harajuku Bakehouse is a quick-service format offering Japanese breads, desserts and savoury snacks. The company has developed its menu and operating platform with chefs Asami Indo and Higuchi Nariaki to support expansion and introduce contemporary Japanese food to Indian consumers.
Over the next two quarters, Harajuku plans to open 10 outlets across new neighbourhoods in Delhi NCR and Mumbai. It also plans to enter Bengaluru and Chandigarh. The company aims to operationalise central kitchens in Mumbai and Bengaluru by December 2026. These facilities will supply Harajuku Bakehouse outlets and support the production of its packaged food range for western and southern India.
Since its seed funding round in August 2025, the company has doubled its outlet count and revenue. Mumbai, where the brand launched in July 2025, now contributes 25% of its revenue. Harajuku processes more than 1,000 orders per day across dine-in and delivery channels.
Harajuku Bakehouse contributes over 30% of the company’s total revenue. In Delhi NCR, its products record sales of more than 1,000 loaves of bread per week on quick commerce platform Blinkit. The company plans to expand its Bakehouse presence to additional metropolitan markets.

Bluestone’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 745 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 514 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.

For the first half of FY27, Bluestone’s revenue from operations increased 47.3% to Rs 1,482 crore from Rs 1,006 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Income from the sale of jewellery remained the company’s primary source of revenue. The company also recorded Rs 24 crore in income apart from revenue from operations, taking its total income to Rs 769 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 525 crore in Q2 FY26. In Q1 FY27, total income stood at Rs 752 crore.
On the expenditure front, the cost of materials remained the largest cost centre at Rs 470 crore, up 51.4% year-on-year. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 70.58 crore, while finance costs and depreciation expenses stood at Rs 58.37 crore and Rs 63.87 crore, respectively.
Overall, Bluestone’s total expenditure increased 34% to Rs 772 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 576 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, expenditure rose from Rs 745 crore in Q1 FY27.
At the bottom line, BlueStone narrowed its net loss by 91.6% to Rs 4.37 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 52 crore in Q2 FY26. The company had posted a profit of around Rs 6 crore in Q1 FY27.
The Bengaluru-based company reported a net profit of Rs 1.59 crore in H1 FY27, compared to a net loss of Rs 86.85 crore in H1 FY26.

In September 2026, BlueStone appointed CarDekho Group CEO and co-founder Amit Jain as a Non-Executive Independent Director.
At the end of the trading session, BlueStone shares closed at Rs 760.45 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 11,305 crore.

title: Ultraviolette launches X-47 Venom electric motorcycle, introduces new VX-100 platform
summary:
Bengaluru-based electric mobility startup Ultraviolette Automotive has launched the X-47 Venom electric motorcycle alongside a new 100V VX-100 platform. The motorcycle is priced at Rs 2.65 lakh under an introductory offer, with deliveries scheduled to begin in November 2026.
The X-47 Venom is the first motorcycle built on Ultraviolette’s new VX-100 architecture. The company said the platform is designed to improve performance, energy efficiency, charging speed and safety while reducing vehicle weight.
Bookings for the motorcycle open on October 22, with the introductory price applicable to the first 5,000 customers. The vehicle will be available across India through Ultraviolette’s UV Space Stations.
The X-47 Venom offers an IDC-certified range of 343 km, a peak power output of 30 kW (40 hp) and a top speed of 155 kmph. It can accelerate from 0 to 60 kmph in 2.7 seconds and from 0 to 100 kmph in 5.9 seconds. The motorcycle delivers 550 Nm of torque at the wheel and has a kerb weight of 180 kg, which is up to 20 kg lower than that of the previous-generation platform, according to the company.
The motorcycle supports 12 kW DC fast charging and comes with a 1.6 kW onboard charger. Ultraviolette claims it is the only electric two-wheeler in India to support 12 kW DC fast charging.
“The X-47 Venom brings these advances to life, combining distinctive design with deeper engineering capabilities and technology that enhances the riding experience,” said Narayan Subramaniam, CEO and co-founder of Ultraviolette.
The VX-100 platform integrates the company’s SRB-11 battery technology, UV LIGHTFURY motor and a next-generation motor control unit. Ultraviolette said the battery technology offers up to 20% higher energy density and twice the cooling performance. An optimised thermal management system is designed to dissipate heat up to 50% faster.
The battery pack also features a pyro-fuse designed to isolate the electrical circuit within microseconds when a critical fault is detected. It works alongside a battery management system that monitors cell-level voltage, temperature and current, as well as individual cell fuses.
The motorcycle features a 77 GHz rear radar system under the company’s UV Hypersense technology. The system supports blind-spot monitoring, lane-change assistance, overtake alerts and rear-collision warnings.
Other features include a seven-inch TFT touchscreen, cruise control, park assist with a rear-camera feed, Mappls-integrated navigation and connectivity through the VIOLETTE A.I. system.
Alongside the motorcycle, Ultraviolette has introduced B-MAX, a reusable rider safety vest designed to extend its safety features beyond the vehicle. The company claims the vest provides 86% force attenuation and can be reused up to five times.
Commenting on the motorcycle’s engineering, Niraj Rajmohan, CTO and co-founder of Ultraviolette, said the VX-100 architecture, battery technology, lighter motor and motor control unit had been developed as an integrated system to improve power delivery, efficiency, thermal performance and safety.
The modular VX-100 platform is also designed to support different battery capacities, vehicle configurations and power levels across Ultraviolette’s future product portfolio.
Founded in 2016 by Narayan Subramaniam and Niraj Rajmohan, Ultraviolette develops electric vehicle platforms and battery technologies. The company is backed by investors including Lingotto, TDK Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures, Zoho Corporation, TVS Motor Company, Yali Capital and Speciale Invest.
Ultraviolette said it has expanded its presence to 20 countries across Europe. The company plans to launch the X-47 Venom in Europe on November 3 at EICMA 2026 in Milan, Italy.

title: Binny Bansal-backed ShopOS launches AI creative platform Sloosh
summary:
ShopOS, a Bengaluru-based AI startup backed by Flipkart co-founder Binny Bansal’s 3STATE Ventures, has launched Sloosh.ai, an AI creative platform that generates product images, visual scenes, reels and creator-style videos from ideas, photos and videos.
The launch comes after ShopOS raised $20 million from 3STATE Ventures. The startup provides AI-powered creative production for fashion, retail and direct-to-consumer brands across India, the UAE and the US.
Sloosh uses the same image and video orchestration engine that ShopOS deploys for brand clients. The platform combines AI agents, reusable workflows and human expertise to help creators, agencies, founders and small businesses produce content across formats.
The platform offers four ways to create content: an AI chat interface, ready-made workflows called Spaces, a visual workflow builder called Spacelab, and assistance from ShopOS’s in-house creative team. Its batch mode can generate hundreds of images and videos through reusable workflows.
Sloosh also connects with AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Cursor through its Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration. The company is also launching a plugin for Adobe After Effects.
Founded by Sai Krishna V K and Ajay P V, ShopOS was built by the team behind Scapic, an AI and augmented reality commerce platform acquired by Flipkart in 2020. The founders later set up and led Flipkart Labs.
Sloosh is available globally, with new accounts receiving 20 free credits and paid plans starting at $19 per month.
